questions.prompt: What does `@tailrec` annotation (`scala.annotation.tailrec`) enforce on a recursive method?

options.text: Verifies at compile time that the method is tail-recursive so the compiler compiles it into a constant-stack-space loop (preventing `StackOverflowError`)

code.source: @tailrec def sum(xs: List[Int], acc: Int = 0): Int = ...

questions.prompt: Why does `scala.concurrent.Future { ... }` execute immediately when constructed rather than lazily?

options.text: `Future` is an eager handle to an already-started computation on an `ExecutionContext` (unlike lazy effect types such as Cats Effect `IO` or `ZIO`)
It runs on the calling thread always

questions.prompt: Why must blocking I/O inside `Future` NOT run directly on `ExecutionContext.global` without `scala.concurrent.blocking { ... }` (or a dedicated I/O pool)?

options.text: Blocking calls starve the CPU-sized `ForkJoinPool` threads; `blocking { ... }` hints the pool to spawn/compensate threads (or better, use a dedicated bounded blocking `ExecutionContext`)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `TypeTag` / `ClassTag` and JVM type erasure in Scala. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `ClassTag[T]` captures the runtime `Class[_]` of `T` (needed for `Array.empty[T]` or `case x: T` runtime class checks)
In Scala 3, `Matchable` warns when pattern-matching on completely unconstrained generic `Any` values
JVM bytecode preserves full nested `List[String]` vs `List[Int]` runtime types without `TypeTag`
Generic type arguments `T` in `def isList[T](x: Any)` are erased at runtime on the JVM

questions.prompt: Match each Scala type-class or contextual pattern to its role.

columns.label: Ad-hoc type class providing `compare(a, b)` for `.sorted` / `TreeSet`
Preserves runtime class info for allocating generic `Array[T]`
Opts into multiversal strict equality (`strictEquality`) preventing nonsensical `1 == "1"`

questions.prompt: What does `Promise[T]` provide in `scala.concurrent`?

options.text: A writable, single-assignment container whose `.success(v)` / `.failure(e)` completes an associated read-only `promise.future` (ideal for bridging callback APIs)

questions.prompt: Why is `Await.result(fut, 5.seconds)` discouraged inside async/server request paths?

options.text: It blocks the calling thread while waiting, risking thread-pool starvation and deadlocks; compose with `.map`/`.flatMap` or `Future.sequence` instead

questions.prompt: What does `Future.sequence(listOfFutures)` do?

options.text: Transforms `List[Future[A]]` into `Future[List[A]]` (completing when all succeed, or failing fast on the first failure)
Runs futures one by one sequentially

questions.prompt: What is `LazyList` (`#::`, Scala 2.13+/3, replacing `Stream`)?

options.text: A lazy, memoized sequence whose tail is only computed on demand (careful: holding a `val` reference to the head retains all evaluated elements in RAM!)

questions.prompt: How does `Iterator[T]` differ from `LazyList[T]`?

options.text: `Iterator` is stateful and single-pass ($O(1)$ memory, exhausted after traversal); `LazyList` is immutable and memoizes evaluated nodes

questions.prompt: What does `inline` in Scala 3 (`inline def check(inline cond: Boolean)`) enable?

options.text: Guaranteed compile-time expansion/inlining, enabling zero-overhead abstractions, `inline if` dead-branch elimination, and Scala 3 macros

questions.prompt: What is the 'type class' pattern in Scala?

options.text: Defining a generic trait `trait Show[A]` and providing `given` (implicit) instances per type `A`, enabling retroactive extension without modifying `A`

questions.prompt: What is 'implicit/given scope' resolution order risk when defining orphan `given` instances?

options.text: Defining a `given` outside the companion objects of the type class or target type requires explicit imports and can cause ambiguity if two packages define conflicting instances

questions.prompt: Select all benefits of pure functional effect systems (like Cats Effect `IO` or `ZIO`) over `scala.concurrent.Future` in large Scala backends. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Referential transparency: an `IO` value is a lazy description of a program, not an already-running side effect
Built-in structured concurrency, fiber cancellation, and `Resource` bracket safety
Explicit typed error channels (e.g. `ZIO[R, E, A]`) and dependency wiring
Forces every operation onto a single OS thread with no parallelism

questions.prompt: What does `Future.recoverWith` do vs `Future.recover`?

options.text: `recover` maps a `Throwable` to a synchronous fallback value `A`; `recoverWith` maps a `Throwable` to an asynchronous `Future[A]` (e.g. retry or fallback call)

questions.prompt: What is `String` / `Collection` `.par` (`scala-parallel-collections`) pitfall when mixed with shared mutable `var`s?

options.text: Mutating a non-synchronized `var` or mutable `Map` inside `.par.foreach` causes classic multi-threaded race conditions and lost updates

questions.prompt: What does `scala.util.control.NonFatal(e)` match in a `catch` block?

options.text: Exceptions that are safe to catch and recover from, excluding fatal JVM errors (`OutOfMemoryError`, `VirtualMachineError`, `InterruptedException`)

questions.prompt: What is `TASTy` in Scala 3?

options.text: Typed Abstract Syntax Trees stored alongside `.class` files, enabling cross-version binary compatibility, macros, and whole-program inspection

questions.prompt: What does `scala.collection.immutable.ArraySeq` (Scala 2.13+/3) wrap cleanly?

options.text: An immutable wrapper around a JVM `Array` providing $O(1)$ indexing, primitive specialization, and value-safe immutability

questions.prompt: Match each Scala engineering tool or idiom to its purpose.

columns.label: Automated code formatting and AST-based refactoring/linting
Detects binary-incompatible ABI changes in published libraries
Property-based testing generating randomized edge-case inputs

questions.prompt: What does `sealed abstract class` vs `sealed trait` offer when binary compatibility on the JVM matters?

options.text: `sealed abstract class` can preserve constructor/method ABI better across versions and be easier to call from Java

questions.prompt: What is a 'magnet pattern' or 'type-level' pitfall of overusing implicit conversions (`Conversion[A, B]`)?

options.text: Implicit conversions hide control flow, produce confusing type errors, and can trigger unexpected allocations; Scala 3 requires `import scala.language.implicitConversions`

questions.prompt: What does `scala.util.boundary` / `boundary.break(val)` (Scala 3.3+) replace?

options.text: Legacy `NonLocalReturn` / `Breaks` exceptions with a cleaner, structured early-return mechanism

questions.prompt: What does `Matchable` trait in Scala 3 guard against?

options.text: Pattern-matching on opaque/abstract types (`Any`) whose runtime representation might violate parametricity or Java interop assumptions

questions.prompt: Select all practices that keep Scala compile times fast in large codebases. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Put every file in one giant 10,000-line `Main.scala` with inferred public return types
Annotate explicit return types on public methods and `given`s
Keep implicit/given search scopes small and avoid deeply nested type-level macro derivations on huge DTOs
Modularize builds into focused `sbt` subprojects so incremental compilation (Zinc) recompiles less

questions.prompt: What does `Future.unit` or `Future.successful(val)` avoid compared to `Future { val }`?

options.text: Avoids scheduling a task onto the `ExecutionContext` thread pool when the value is already computed synchronously

code.source: if cached then Future.successful(hit) else fetchRemote(id)

questions.prompt: What does `scala.collection.mutable.Builder` (e.g., `List.newBuilder[Int]`) optimize?

options.text: Building immutable collections (`List`, `Vector`, `ArraySeq`) in loops in $O(n)$ time without repeated `+:`/`.+` copies

questions.prompt: What happens when `case class` `apply` or `unapply` is overloaded or `private` constructor is used (`case class Email private (value: String)`)?

options.text: In Scala 3, `private` primary constructor also makes `copy` and `apply` private unless a smart constructor `Email.from(s)` is provided

questions.prompt: What does `IArray[T]` (Scala 3) provide over `Array[T]`?

options.text: An opaque, zero-overhead *immutable* array wrapper that prevents accidental element mutation while keeping JVM array performance

questions.prompt: What is a 'ghost' / phantom type parameter pattern (`StateMachine[Locked]` vs `StateMachine[Unlocked]`)?

options.text: A type parameter `S` not stored at runtime that enforces valid state transitions at compile time (typestate pattern)

questions.prompt: What does `-Wunused:all` / `-Xfatal-warnings` (or `-Werror` in Scala 3) enforce in CI?

options.text: Fails builds on unused imports, unused locals, dead code, and non-exhaustive matches

questions.prompt: What does `scala.util.control.NoStackTrace` on custom domain error classes optimize?

options.text: Skips expensive JVM `fillInStackTrace()` capture when an exception is used purely for expected control/error signaling

questions.prompt: Match each Scala concurrency/collection pitfall to its fix.
What does `summon[Ordering[Int]]` (Scala 3, replacing `implicitly`) do?

options.text: Retrieves the `given` instance of `Ordering[Int]` currently in scope at compile time

questions.prompt: What does `Either.catchNonFatal` (Cats) or `Try(...).toEither` accomplish?

options.text: Converts exception-throwing Java/legacy blocks into composable `Either[Throwable, A]` values

questions.prompt: Why is `Option.when(cond)(expr)` preferred over `if (cond) Some(expr) else None`?

options.text: More concise and lazy in `expr` (only evaluates `expr` when `cond` is `true`)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `Union` (`A | B`) and `Intersection` (`A & B`) types in Scala 3. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Union types work cleanly with exhaustive `match`
Union types require runtime boxing in an `Either` wrapper always
`Int | String` accepts either an `Int` or a `String` without wrapping in `Either`
`Readable & Closeable` requires a value to implement both traits (replacing Scala 2 `with` in types)

questions.prompt: What does `using` clause with `ExecutionContext` (`def fetch(id: Long)(using ec: ExecutionContext): Future[User]`) communicate?

options.text: `fetch` performs async composition and lets the caller control which thread pool executes its callbacks

questions.prompt: What does `Future.firstCompletedOf(Seq(workFut, timeoutFut))` implement?

options.text: Racing a computation against a timeout future, completing with whichever finishes first

questions.prompt: What does `scala.util.Using.Manager { use => ... }` solve when acquiring multiple resources conditionally or in a loop?

options.text: Registers multiple `AutoCloseable` resources via `use(res)` and closes all of them in reverse order when the block exits

questions.prompt: Select all best practices for designing maintainable Scala libraries. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Prefer immutable collections and pure functions, pushing I/O/effects to the edges
Test invariants with property-based tests (ScalaCheck) alongside unit tests
Use `null`, `var`, and `asInstanceOf` casts throughout public APIs
Model domain states with closed ADTs (`enum` / `sealed trait`) and `opaque type`s

questions.prompt: Why is `asInstanceOf[T]` discouraged in Scala except inside tightly encapsulated low-level code?

options.text: It bypasses static type safety and throws `ClassCastException` at runtime if wrong (prefer pattern matching `match` instead)
